verification.funding_note: A four-year full-tuition scholarship plus fully-funded, GPSP-sponsored summer programs. No cash stipend or dollar value is published.
verification.covered_expenses: Full tuition and fully-funded, GPSP-sponsored summer programs. Housing, food, travel and living stipends are not stated.
eligibility: Only candidates for fall admission are considered; transfers are not eligible
Early Decision and Regular Decision applicants who submit their Boston College applications by the November 1 priority scholarship deadline
18 incoming freshman students are selected each year
Students are selected for leadership character and outstanding scholarship; they enroll in one of the University's departmental honors programs
required_docs: Boston College undergraduate application (Common Application) submitted by the November 1 priority scholarship deadline
No separate application, essays, or additional materials are required for the program
verification.deadline_note: Boston College's published priority scholarship deadline is November 1 (2026-11-01 for the current cycle); Early Decision and Regular Decision applicants who apply by that date are considered for the program's 18 annual seats. Confirm the date for your entry cycle with Boston College admission.
verification.application_process: There is no separate application: prospective students submit their Boston College application by the November 1 priority deadline, and the Gabelli Presidential Scholars Program considers those applicants for fall admission. Scholars enroll in a departmental honors program and participate in the program's summer and yearly curriculum.
verification.contact_info: Gabelli Presidential Scholars Program, Boston College, Chestnut Hill, MA; info.gpsp@bc.edu
verification.status_note: Verified on bc.edu (Gabelli Presidential Scholars Program pages), retrieved 2026-10-10. The program has operated each year since 1991; its pillars are Global Leadership, Hospitality, Fidelity to Partners and Promoting the Common Good, and scholars complete fully-funded summer programs in service learning, international experience and professional internships, plus a weekly Tuesday evening program.

applicant_utility.exciting_but_honest_wins: For eighteen people a year, Boston College's most prestigious scholarship removes tuition for all four years and funds three summers outright: a service-learning summer in Boston-area organizations, international trips to Europe, Latin America and the Middle East, and a junior-summer professional internship anywhere from Wall Street to Bangkok. Scholars also join a departmental honors program with weekly seminar evenings - it is a leadership cohort, not a cheque.
applicant_utility.good_fit_if: You are a strong senior applying to Boston College who wants the formational Jesuit experience more than a cash stipend, and who can genuinely commit to a program with mandatory service, international and professional components across four summers. You do not need to apply Early Decision to be considered, which makes it rare among full-ride caliber programmes at peer schools.
applicant_utility.potential_drawbacks: Eighteen seats for an entire class makes it one of the most selective small programmes in US higher education, and the award is tuition-only - room, board and flights to the summer programs are your expense. The program's structure is intensive by design: weekly meetings, four summers of programming, an honors thesis. If you only wanted money, this is the wrong scholarship; if your summers are already spoken for, that can conflict.
document_checklist: Boston College Common Application by November 1 (priority scholarship deadline)
Strong academic record aligned with a departmental honors program fit
No separate GPSP forms, essays, or named references are requested
Evidence of sustained leadership and service if the admission office asks for supplements
applicant_utility.playbook_for_working_applicants: Your application must show a real spine of service and leadership, because the program screens applicants' character, not a separate essay. Apply by November 1 and do not assume an Early Decision requirement - ED is not needed, so keep options open. When writing the BC supplements, foreground experiences that map onto the program's four summers: community service, language learning and an internship arc. Email info.gpsp@bc.edu with questions about demonstrated interest, and prepare a family budget that subtracts four years of tuition but still covers living costs and summer travel, since only the tuition and program summers are funded.
